questions.q: What is the article mainly about?
options: CEOs ousted over relationships, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang
Nvidia's chip strategy and how its board reviews executive pay
How boards reformed governance rules after the Me Too movement
Founders who were fired and later returned to lead their firms
questions.explain: It places Huang's resignation among other CEOs ousted over affairs and personal conduct.

questions.q: What was unusual about the Huang case compared with typical CEO ousters?
options: Nvidia's code of conduct had no policy on personal relationships
He had led Nvidia for only a few months before he was forced out
A woman he was involved with was judged an intelligence asset for China
He was dismissed by the board rather than resigning of his own accord
questions.explain: Intelligence agencies concluded one woman was an asset for China.

questions.q: How much did Steve Easterbrook give back to McDonald's?
options: More than $10 million
More than $25 million
More than $50 million
More than $105 million
questions.explain: He gave back more than $105 million in cash and stock.

questions.q: How long was Sam Altman out as OpenAI's chief executive in 2023?
options: Five days
One month
Two weeks
Five months
questions.explain: He was pushed out on a Friday and reinstated five days later.

questions.q: What does Sonnenfeld's remark that the board "has taken too long" imply?
options: Boards should never fire founders of very successful companies
Boards defer to successful founders and may ignore warning signs
Huang resigned too early, before the board could complete its review
Boards are unaware of the conduct rules their chief executives follow
questions.explain: He says boards are in awe of founders and there were lots of indicators for a board paying attention.
